issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a condition such as C>2 (or choose Ω_ρ to exclude all tail poles) and restate the main LP results for sufficiently large fixed C; the advertised rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for all α>0, but the displayed proof bound uses 1−α and C^{1−α} rather than the fractional-part quantity 1−(α). For α>1 the factor 1−α is negative and the C-power is not the one established earlier, so the displayed estimate cannot upper-bound the positive error norm as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1−α by 1−(α) and C^{1−α} by C^{1−(α)} in the derivation of \eqref{rat01}, or restrict the theorem to 0<α<1.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem mainthm, and downstream results relying on it, does not establish the claimed all-α>0 rate.
issues.title: Proof of main theorem uses 1−α instead of fractional part for α>1
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local notation fix supported by the earlier bound and does not require new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Runge's theorem requires f to be analytic on a neighborhood of K (or on an open set containing K). The hypothesis “analytic on K” alone is insufficient, so the stated theorem is false or ill-defined as a supporting result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that f is analytic in a neighborhood of K.
issues.overall_effect: Every polynomial-approximation step invoking this theorem (tail approximation for the LPs and approximation of g in the generalized results) lacks a correctly stated supporting result.
issues.title: Runge theorem stated with missing neighborhood hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis repair restores the standard theorem; the intended applications already supply the needed analyticity in context.

issues.failure_explanation: The even extension \bar f is nonzero at the origin and at the endpoints, so the identity relating the full-line Poisson sum to 2(I−r_{N_t}) omits local terms. Moreover, for a general hbar that is an integer multiple of h, the reflected Fourier integral has coefficient 1/h, not 1/hbar. Thus the derivation of the quadrature-error estimate is not valid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the Fourier-coefficient bookkeeping and the Poisson-sum identity by including and uniformly bounding the local center terms; this is a contained re-derivation of the standard sinc/trapezoidal argument.
issues.overall_effect: The quadrature-error theorem, and hence the root-exponential convergence claims built on it, are not established by the supplied proof.
issues.title: Quadrature-error proof has inconsistent even-extension/Poisson bookkeeping
issues.why_classification: The repair is local to the central proof but requires nontrivial correction of the Poisson/contour bookkeeping and uniform bounding of extra local terms, more than a one-line typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The rest of the paper and the proof use σ_opt=π√{2(2−β)}/√α. The stated value is larger by √2, so the piecewise thresholds and the claimed optimal rate at σ=σ_opt are inconsistent: at the stated σ_opt the first branch would give e^{-2π√{(2−β)αN}}, not the intended e^{-π√{2(2−β)αN}}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor 2√{2−β} by √{2(2−β)} (equivalently π√{2(2−β)}/√α) in the definition of σ_opt in mainthmG.
issues.overall_effect: The generalized theorem mainthmG states a false optimal parameter/rate; the corner-domain theorem that invokes mainthmG is affected until the parameter is corrected.
issues.title: Generalized theorem states wrong optimal sigma by a factor of sqrt 2
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction supported by the proof and other statements restores the intended result without loss.
